history.dynasty: Maratha reconstruction by Maloji Bhosale (16th century) and Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore (18th century); original temple traditionally 13th century
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 609 ('Grishneshwar Temple', id grishneshwar-temple-aurangabad) - same real temple. Grishneshwar at Verul, near the Ellora Caves about 30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), is the 12th and last of the Jyotirlingas of Shiva, the name meaning 'lord of compassion'. The original temple is traditionally dated to the 13th century and was destroyed during the Delhi Sultanate incursions of the 13th-14th centuries, then went through repeated cycles of rebuilding and re-destruction during the Mughal-Maratha conflicts. Reconstructed by Maloji Bhosale of Verul (grandfather of Chhatrapati Shivaji) in the 16th century, it was rebuilt in its present form in the 18th century under Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore. The central legend: the devout Ghushma, whose son was murdered, continued her Shiva worship unshaken; Shiva manifested here as a Jyotirlinga and, at her request, remained for the welfare of devotees. Built in red volcanic stone with a five-tier shikhara, it shows Maratha-style architecture with intricate carvings including Dashavatara panels. Completing the twelve-Jyotirlinga yatra here is seen as the fulfilment of a lifetime vow.

name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Verul (also spelled Verul) is the village adjoining the Ellora Caves in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district, Maharashtra, about 30 km northwest of the city. It is best known as the home of the Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga, which stands about 1 km from the cave complex, making Verul a major twin pilgrimage destination with the UNESCO World Heritage Ellora Caves. The village also carries Maratha history as the ancestral home of Maloji Bhosale, grandfather of Chhatrapati Shivaji.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Airport, approx. 30 km; taxis and app cabs available.
travel.railway: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Railway Station, approx. 30 km, well connected to Mumbai and Pune; autos and taxis to Verul.
travel.road: About 30 km northwest of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on the Aurangabad-Ellora road; regular MSRTC and private buses, autos and taxis run to Ellora/Verul. Ellora Caves about 1 km away; Ajanta Caves about 100 km.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri and Shravan month are the most significant times but very crowded; weekday early mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx. 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM daily (verify - some sources list 5:00 AM opening; Shravan month extended timings approx. 3:00 AM-11:00 PM). Free entry. Traditional dress advised. Men must go bare-chested to enter the garbhagriha sanctum; leather items, cameras and mobile phones are restricted inside.
